utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All accused are here. Prosecution, same as yesterday. Defence, I notice the absence of Ms. Tapuskovic, Ms. Nikolic, Mr. Krgovic. That's it. Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic will continue and finish his cross-examination, and then we'll see who goes next. Thank you. Good morning to you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And especially good morning to you, Mr. Janc. I hope you had an opportunity to rest, and I assure you that we are going to finish today pursuant to the instruction given to the Presiding Judge, His Honour Judge Agius. We are going to pick up where we left off yesterday, but I indicated that we are going to move on to a new topic, so let's proceed. As an OTP investigator, you are, of course, aware that after the 13th, and we all know that that's when the Kravica incident happened, there were pockets of Muslims in Srebrenica, Bratunac, and Milici who failed to break through with the column towards Tuzla; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I also assume that you are aware that after the 13th of July on several occasions, the ground was scoured in order to neutralise the Muslims groups that remained behind. I suppose that you are also aware of that as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us just go briefly through documents that relate to this topic. I have reduced the number of the documents that I originally intended to show you to only a small number, but the ones that I'm going to show you are characteristic of the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let's look at document 4D5251. That's the order of the Bratunac Brigade commander for the search of the terrain. The Exhibit is 4DP251. As I said, that's the order issued by the Bratunac Brigade commander to search the terrain of 14th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Items 1 and 2 and 3 clearly show that on the 14th of July, the infantry battalion of the brigade received an order to search the terrain and that they were given precise access along which they were supposed to do that. I think that this document clearly shows this.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to next document. That's P4372.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to appear in e-court, that's a document sent by Colonel Ignjat Milatovic from the Drina Corps sent on the 15th of July. In the first passage, you can see in the letter in front of you is in the process of searching the area that had been ordered, and in the bottom part of the document you see where it says proposal, item 1 reads that the commander -- or it has been suggested that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade be authorised appointed commander of all forces engaged in the search of the terrain and the assignation of the battle-field east of the road and within the road between Kasaba and the Drinjaca. I will just make it clear that this is the Milici-Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road that he is talking about here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at the next document, and that's 4DP255. Can we please just find the time and date, and in the bottom right-hand corner you can see that this document is dated 16th July, 1995, and then can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a regular combat report issued by the Bratunac Brigade on the 16th of July, 1995. What we can see from it under item 2, it is clearer in English because this handwriting is not very legible. It says there the forces of the Bratunac Brigade are still engaged in scouring the terrain in the zone that had been ordered. And if we can just look down, scroll down so that we can see better, we see that the Bratunac Brigade commander -- and if we can zoom in the bottom part in B/C/S, please. It says that the Bratunac Brigade command during that day - therefore, we are speaking about the 16th of July - reviewed all the units blocking the pullout of the enemy, and he mentioned the Milici Brigade, a unit of the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment, and some other units, and he gave more detailed tasks and organised a coordinated action and communication. This is what we can see from this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Obviously, we can conclude from this document that on the 16th of July, the searching of terrain and the blocking of the Muslim forces trying to pull through towards Tuzla is still in progress. That is what this document shows.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I would like you to look at is P257. If we can just turn this side around because it's upside-down, the one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On this first page, we see that the document was delivered - that's what it says - on the 18th of July, 1995, at 0040 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we can now move to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, the first sentence in this document indicates that the Bratunac Brigade among its prisoners has two underage children.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Four underage children.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just confirm that this is what this document reads?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the prisoners mentioned in this document and in the previous document were the outcome of the search of the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now move to the next document, which is P1185. While we're waiting for this document to come up, I will tell you that this is an intercept of 17th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are being informed that it's not yet in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to my information, this should already be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P1185, if the number is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The number is correct, so it should be in e-court because it's a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is, but there are letters that follow these intercept numbers, so he should refer whether he is saying A, B, C, most likely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see, I see. Okay. Thank you. And that means the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we should add A to this number, and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. B. Found it? Yes. Being is the English version. A, English. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to identify, we see in the middle of the page number 653. The date is the 17th of July, 1995, and I'm talking about the middle portion of this intercept, which is marked 653. The participants in this conversation have not been identified, and you see that the first portion of the sentence is missing, but there is mention of Kravica, though, but from the content of this intercept one can see that one of the speakers talks about an order from the Superior Command to carry out the sanitation and hygiene measures and that not a shred of cloth should remain behind. I think that you can see that from this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, we are talking about the 17th. Do you know, or did you find any information that this assignation of the terrain was indeed conducted on the 17th of July? If you can help us with that, and with further documents and further discussions we are going to go into more detail, but for now, tell me, do you know whether this assignation was conducted on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what we can see here, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. If we can now look at the following document. It's 4DP263. And if we can go immediately to page 3 in B/C/S and page 1 in English, it is a regular combat report of the Bratunac Brigade for the 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this report it says, as you can see, that units of the Bratunac Brigade are persistently pursuing and destroying the remaining enemy groups and that the second infantry Battalion is engaged in scouring the ground around Gornji Potocari, Bljeceva, Cizmici -- let me just repeat: Gornji Potocari, Bljeceva, Cizmici, Leovici, and Bacuta; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is obvious that on the 19th of July, the search of the ground is still going on precisely in the area that we had discussed; this is Bljeceva, Gornji Potocari, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to make this examination short, and I'm not going to go with you through all the documents relating to the search of the ground, but only for the record, I would like the number of exhibits to be recorded, and I'm going to read this for transcript. This is Exhibit 4D596, P527 [as interpreted], 4DP262, 4DP263, 4D529, 4DP265, and 5266 [as interpreted]. All these documents have already been admitted into evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us keep a period of time and move immediately to document 4D755. This is another document issued by the Bratunac Brigade commander ordering the troops to search the area of the former Zepa enclave, and the date is the 13th of August, 1995. This document apparently shows that units of the Bratunac Brigade were obviously engaged in August 1995 in the search of terrain around the Zepa enclave, and what this document indicates is something that gives us a different time-line. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us summarise what we have seen from all these documents. Based on these documents, can we conclude that the search of the ground was an ongoing activity conducted in the period from 14th of July onwards, as well as in August 1995, which we have seen in the documents just now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, there are numerous testimonies about this, and there is evidence that members of the BH were actually killed in the course of this operation. I think you have come across documents showing that men were killed in the process.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We had occasion through some of these documents that we were just discussing to see or come across the term "asanacija." Since I am a layperson and I'm not very versed in military terminology, do we understand and perceive this term in the same way, and that is bury the human remains and carcasses in order to prevent any widespread of contagious diseases? Is that how you understand this term "asanacija"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand it like that. That's what I have learned here during the trial. But I think we have seen this term to be used only once as proposal in these documents you have shown me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I just wanted to establish that we understand this term "asanacija," sanitisation, in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I would like to look at is P220. It's the diary of the duty officer of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, and can we look the a page 21 in B/C/S; that is page 18 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps to put this in a time context -- and we don't see the date on this page. I think -- yes. All right. We have what we need. But we don't see the date on the page itself, so perhaps it would be good to look at the previous page in B/C/S to find out at what time this was happening. On the previous page, we see an entry for the 18th, and this is the following page, so we think it's the 19th. Now we see the previous page. The entry is dated 18 July, and logically, therefore, the following page should be the 19th. In the page I originally asked for in B/C/S, we can see that the patrols of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, obviously, went to provide security for utility companies personnel in Glogova. Does this entry tell you that on the 19th, employees of the public utility service carried out burials in Glogova and that this unit of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade went to that location to be their security detail?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From these documents you can see that something was going on there but not exactly what, so we can just assume that there were still reburials or some work related to this issue was going on, but what exactly, we can't see from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course it's not explicitly written in the document that these utility workers were digging graves in Glogova, but I suppose your proposition is very reasonable as to what this could be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I'd like to look at is P3016.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's an order from the Drina Corps of the 20th July, 1995, sent to all subordinated units concerning the sanitisation of the battle-field in the zone of responsibility of individual units. In the introductory part, we see which units there are, and then let's look at items 1, 2, and 3 of the order. Did you manage to look through?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude on the basis of this document that even after the 19th, the date we saw on the previous document, the order obligating all units of the Drina Corps to carry out sanitisation of the terrain in their respective areas of responsibility was still in effect.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, it says that in cooperation with the civilian protection health centres and hospitals, these units have to carry out sanitisation in their areas of responsibility, focusing on Srebrenica and Zepa areas and axis roads leading to these areas from Bosnia. That is a wider area; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It also says that work crews are being formed with the necessary amount of personnel and materiel, trucks, tractors with trailers, et cetera, and that locations for graves should be immediately designated on the ground to ensure the necessary protective measures. We can read all that here; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My question is, do you know where the bodies of people killed were buried, those people who were found in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac or the Milici Brigade, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So what we don't know in this respect is the number of people killed in the course of search of terrain, the number of bodies collected during sanitisation, or where those bodies were buried. You have no knowledge about that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we don't have any knowledge about how many of them have been collected, how many of them killed. We just have knowledge how many of them stayed on the ground, how many of them have been picked up during these years in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. And, of course, we can reasonably assume that the bodies that were found in that area were buried in the graves in Glogova; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't conclude that. That would be speculation. I know for some of the bodies -- or for some of the people who are found during this search of the terrain, that the bodies were found in Cerska grave. So from the document you showed me from the 17th when you were -- which is talking about the underage children, we have a statement from, I think, two of those kids, and one of them has named four individuals which were captured in area of Bornica [phoen] around 17 of July, and then their bodies showed up in Cerska grave. So some of them -- for some of them which were captured during these days during the search of terrain, we know where did they end up but not for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are also aware of that fact, and I know very well what you are talking about. You are talking about individuals who are captured, and those four bodies were found in Cerska, so the total number is four. What I'm asking you, however, is can you rule out the possibility that the bodies of people who were killed during the sanitisation operation were buried among other places in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot rule out this possibility. But as I have told you yesterday, you know, early media shows that most of the work with Glogova was ended by 17 of July, so what was going on between 17 and 27, we have just two new small graves, smaller graves, so with 12 and 6 individuals in it, so that's what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but we'll be using two things. First of all, the aerial images you mentioned do not exist for every single day, do they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they do not. Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And also, if those bodies had been buried in some existing, pre-existing graves, that would not have been observed or noticed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it wouldn't be that easy to observe from the aerial images itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. I'd now like to move on to the next subject. In your corrigendum, you stated that there exist reports and documents that in the Glogova graves ten victims exist, bodies of people who were brought back from Serbia on the 20th, 24th, 26th of July. And you go on to name the documents based on which you gained this knowledge. I won't repeat these documents. We are all aware of them. What I want to ask you is this: You cannot claim, of course, that this is the total number of people who were returned from Serbia to Republika Srpska. You can only say that there are documents from the board of police and from the Bratunac Brigade concerning a certain number of people. There is documentation for this number of people, but we cannot infer that this is the total number of people brought back from Serbia to Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with you that we know just about the cases for which we possess the documents from the authorities. So for the others, we don't know anything, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. That was my point. I'd like to move to the last but one subject of my cross-examination. Let me take you briefly to something that you discussed with Ms. Tapuskovic in her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look again at 1D1368, and please don't broadcast this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a comparative overview of persons that are documented by the BH as having perished before July 1995 with the location of their remains. There is also the number of ICMP protocol under which they are recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also look at page 2, please, because this is an extract prepared by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We see a rubric called ICMP grave-site, and among others we see Ravnice grave, Glogova, Zeleni Jadar. Next page, please. Here we see, among others, Kravica, Bljeceva, and other graves; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, we in the Borovcanin Defence compared information from this list - and this list includes ICMP protocols - with the confidential Annex D from your summary, and we found that all these persons for whom there is an indication of the ICMP protocol are also found in your confidential Annex D. Can you confirm this? I suppose that would require quite a lot of effort and time at this moment, but let us proceed from the assumption that what I said is correct, and I suppose the Prosecution can check this very easily. We took this document and compared the persons from this list, the persons without indication of ICMP protocol - you see that the ICMP protocol is missing for certain individuals on the list - and we compared that with the ICMP missing persons list that was used in the preparation of your report because it was in the form of an Excel sheet which is searchable, and we found 16 persons who do not feature on this list and who from the day when this document was made until the drafting of the ICMP list have been identified. I suppose you cannot tell me this without checking your database, but I'd like to know, did you make such a comparative analysis as we did?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, but I agree with you that there might be some individuals which were identified before the ICMP started their work, so that's why perhaps you found some additional individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when we compared these two lists focusing on the persons who were found and identified in the meantime, we looked at the graves relevant for the Borovcanin Defence, and we found as follows: For Glogova 1, seven cases; Glogova 2, six cases; Ravnice 1 and 2, six cases; Kravica - we're talking about surface remains here, right - five cases; Zeleni Jadar 5, six cases. Zeleni Jadar, six. Let me repeat. Zeleni Jadar 5, six cases. Perhaps if I say this differently. The grave-site is called Zeleni Jadar 5. Then the record will be clear. In this grave, six cases were found. In Zeleni Jadar number 6, there is one case; in Zeleni Jadar number 4, there is one case; in Bljeceva 2, there is one case; and in Bljeceva 3, there are three cases. In total, that gives us the number of 36 persons named in document 1D1368, persons who were identified in these graves. You told me that you did not make this kind of comparative analysis using the document containing information on persons listed by the BH Army as having perished before July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, all these persons feature in Annex D of your summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before Mr. Janc answers, I think a few clarifications are necessary. Comparison of these two lists, it's not clear which comparison of which two lists is being dealt with. The cases that are being mentioned are these connections; and third of all, who are these persons in the questions that was just asked by Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I think a very pertinent comment, particularly the first part of it because I was thinking precisely of the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps if I take you again through the procedure that we followed when making this analysis, maybe that would be of assistance. As a basic document, we took the document we have before us, 1D1368. After that, all the persons that are listed here with an ID protocol of the ICMP with the date July 1995 [as interpreted] were compared with Annex D. Here in the record, it says July 1995. I meant July 2008. And we found that all these persons who have an ID protocol in this document are also in the confidential Annex D attached to the summary of Mr. Janc. That was our first step. The next step, as we can see from this document 1D1368, was to see that there is a certain number of persons who have the blank box of ID protocol of the ICMP and the blank box for grave-site. The names and other information of these persons we compared with the ICMP missing persons list, which was used as a basis for the creation of your Annex D. And in this way, we derived information for another 16 persons who appeared in the meantime on the ICMP missing persons list. I did not mean to use this document. We used it for our internal purposes to derive information for persons who have no personal information indicated in the ICMP document, but this was in the form of an Excel spreadsheet that was searchable. And perhaps we could distribute the hard copies of what we obtained by this search. We have copies for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution. [In English] I don't know whether this explanation clarifies things. I would just like to hear it from my colleagues from the Prosecution. I can see Mr. Janc nodding now. It seems that he understands this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Incidentally, for the record we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis again today. Thank you. Do you wish to comment, Ms. Soljan, or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Not at this time, no, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. What this whole line of cross-examination boils down to is this: For all these persons, there exists information that they died prior to July 1995, but they are still on the ICMP missing persons list related to Srebrenica events of July 1995, and they are also in the confidential Annex D of your report.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'm done with this document. I'd like to look at the next document now without broadcasting it. It's P3159A.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's see the cover page just to see the nature of the document. It's "Srebrenica Missing." The date is 11th July, 1995, and you have had occasion, of course, to see this document before; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 5. I think this will be of assistance. What matters to me are the headings of rubrics.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We see several rubrics concerning information about missing persons, and in column 4 we see date and place of disappearance; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We won't go into each particular entry, but we see that the dates go from 11 July 1995 to 21 July 1995, so we have different dates and different places of disappearance. We also note that Potocari, Buljim, Konjevic Polje, Baljkovica, and various other locations are mentioned in column 4.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this is, of course, information provided by family and friends of the missing persons to the ICMP based on their knowledge when they saw the person alive last, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is incorrect. ICMP did not provide this. This is not found on the ICMP. It's ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. These things happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Anyway, anyway, these are the data provided to the ICRC by the relatives and friends of the missing persons about what they knew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And these data have been entered into this document, which was basically produced by the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This document was not produced by the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She is correct there, as well, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell me who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Indeed. This was the product of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, please. It was a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the witness, not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you in a position to answer Mr. Lazarevic's question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am. This is the product of the OTP. It was created by the demographic unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can challenge their own product, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course it is possible, and I even found the response very useful, but by looking at page 1 of this document, it is called "Progress Report on the DNA Based of the ICMP." That was perhaps the reason for my putting the question as I did. So this is a document produced by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see page 1 out of curiosity. I would like to see it, or the cover. All right. Let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from your answer, I deduce that the OTP had had information, since it made it possible for them to produce this document containing the date and place of disappearance for certain missing persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for us to make a comparison, can we now look at document 53517D. The number should be 3517D. If we can zoom in on this document, please. I'd like to see the right-hand side of the document. That's the document of the ICMP of July -- oh, I'm sorry, this document should not be broadcast because it contains persons' names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Got that, Registrar? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we can look at the right-hand side of the document, it has a total of 11 columns, and let us focus on columns 10 and 11. So column 10 has the heading "Date of Disappearance," and column 11, it has the heading "Place of Disappearance." This is an excerpt from this document. I have went through this whole document. What we see here is that the place of disappearance are only two locations mentioned as such, and that is Suma forest and Potocari. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As for the date of disappearance, it is the 11th of July, 1995, for all the people listed here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: So the OTP had the information from both the ICRC and the ICMP. Of course, it is impossible for all the missing persons to have gone missing on the 11th of July in 1995 either in the forest or in Potocari. Tell me now, this fact that the ICRC information was more complete as to when these persons were last seen alive, did you take this fact into consideration when you were preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. ICRC information or data is more complete, yes, than the ICMP one regarding to date of disappearance because you will find on this -- this is extract from the ICMP list, and you will see that's why the date of disappearance is 11th of July because I think they are putting 11th of July as a fixed date. But on the ICRC list you will find different dates, probably for these same individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, we are talking both about the place and the date of disappearance or, rather, when they were last seen. Right. I'm sorry, I started my next question before waiting for your answer. We are talking about both the place and the date of disappearance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I read very thoroughly your confidential Annex D, and I noticed that the dates and places of disappearance of missing persons do not feature in it at all. Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning of this cross-examinations, you described the methods and what instructions were given and how it came about for you to compile this summary and how you entered the data. Did you yourself make a decision that the information about the place and the date of disappearance of a certain individual should be omitted from your confidential Annex D?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that was my decision, and I apologise for it, but it was simply because of the better resolution when you print out on the screen. If you print out, you know, less columns, then you have better resolution; you can see this data better. So that was the only reason why I did not use that part of it. And as I explained it, date of disappearance within this ICMP list is not that, you know, useful one because I think for most or all of them you will find 11 of July as the date of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that it wouldn't have been very helpful. However, when you made this decision, did you consult anyone from the OTP? Did you tell them this resolution is not good, should I leave this out, or did you do it without consulting anyone at all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was purely my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And nobody from the OTP objected by saying, Look, perhaps we should have this in the report because it provides more information that could be relevant for this case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not remember anyone telling me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us now look at document 4D535 without broadcasting because it contains names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity during your briefing sessions or in some other situation to come across this document? Have you been shown this document by anyone from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then it would be good to -- for me to explain to you what this is. This document has been used on several occasions, and this is a document prepared by Mr. Borovcanin's Defence based on the document 5 -- 3519A, and it refers to the individuals identified in the Glogova graves. We just singled out the individuals where the burial site was Glogova. Now, let us focus on the column that bears the heading "Date and Place of Disappearance."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to avoid going into private session, and for that purpose let us refrain from mentioning any names. We'll just mention the dates and the places of disappearance. Under number 1, we have the date 11th of July, 1995, and the place is Udrc-Zvornik. You know that Udrc near Zvornik, but they are pretty far away from Kravica itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In geographical terms, for someone who would like to walk from one place to another, it's a long walk.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then under 8, it says 18th July, 1995, Kamenica-Bratunac. And the 18th came five days after the 13th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we also have an entry under item 3 where it says 00/07/1995, Kravica-Bratunac, which makes it totally impossible to establish the date in July 1995 when this person was last seen alive. You would agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at all this information and we take them into account, for these persons, either to an uncertain date of their being last seen alive due to the geographical distance from Kravica or the date when they were last seen alive, these persons could not have been the Kravica victims of the incident that took place in July 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In case these -- these data are accurate, then that's the case. But I've seen many of problems so far regarding the exact date and place of disappearance, so that's what we have -- that's why we have, perhaps, a problem. You can't necessarily always rely on this data.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You see, I fully understand what you are saying, so we are starting from the document containing this information that we received from the OTP, and you said this was done by the OTP. Now you are saying that we cannot be sure about this information. My question is, what did the OTP do in order to check any disputable information? Are you aware of anyone from the OTP going out and trying to find out who reported the last sightings of these persons alive, and where were they seen? On what basis do they claim that before that date that person was alive? On the basis of what do they claim that this person on the particular date was in that particular place? Can you tell me this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is based -- this OTP document is based on the ICRC list, and all this work was done by the ICRC. I don't think that OTP has ever checked all of the individuals or any of the individuals regarding this particular issue on why they were reported and how they were reported and by whom they were reported to be last seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, these data were not a basis for the OTP for an investigation that would dispel any dilemmas about what we were just discussing.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because you can find a lot of discrepancies in this data.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I agree. Maybe it won't be necessary for me to go with you through all the documents that I had planned to put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the end, I would just like to ask you to look at one document more, and that's 4D754, and I kindly ask this document not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a similar type of document that we saw a minute ago, the only difference being that this is an excerpt from the Srebrenica missing document updated by Annex D to your report dated 13th March, 2009. That is the persons contained in Bljeceva in your annex have been compared to the Srebrenica missing, and some entries have been added, as you can see here. Therefore, the same dilemma emerges that we had vis-a-vis the previous documents if we take into consideration your Annex D.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might have maybe a couple of more questions and that would be it, but if we can take a break now, I believe I should consult with my client during the break, and it will not take more than five minutes then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That won't entail asking for more time, this consultation, because we have gone well beyond what you have anticipated, so let's try and finish, please, because there are others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break now. We'll start at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's hear the good news, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can assure the Trial Chamber that I can finish in five minutes, literally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janc --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look again at document 4D754 that we already seen, page 1, without it being broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course without mentioning any names, let us clarify a few issues here. Let's look at item 2 where it says 00/07/1995, Kravica-Bratunac. The date is not clear. Actually, we only know the month in which this person was last seen alive, and I can tell you in advance that this kind of information neither confirms nor excludes the possibility that this was a Kravica victim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next entry where it says 18th July, 1995, Konjevic-Polje-Bratunac, and this person was found in Bljeceva-Bratunac. Now, if this entry were correct, it means that this person can be excluded as the Kravica victim due to the date, if we assume that this entry is correct, that is.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: However, there is one more thing that we might deduce from this. Since this person was discovered in Bljeceva and is unrelated to the Kravica incident, this might mean that Bljeceva was for one part a primary grave. It is possible to arrive at that conclusion, as well, again provided this information is correct. Sorry, you were about to give me an answer. If the whole body had been found in the Bljeceva graves and we have information that he wasn't a Kravica victim, that would mean that Bljeceva was partly a primary grave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The counsel should indicate which Bljeceva grave he is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Which Bljeceva grave are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have this piece of information here. Based on this entry 3, I cannot be more specific whether it was Bljeceva 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, and I accept the suggestion put by my learned friend Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If you have in this case the whole body there, this cannot be excluded, but before any conclusions to be made, I would like to -- to see the entire case about it, about this particular individual, meaning the exhumation reports and the autopsy reports and everything. But, yeah, that would be my response.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I fully accept your reply. This would, of course, require additional investigation and checking up of information, and you already told us that this hasn't been done by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my last question refers to document 4D338, and could we please have it in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You haven't. Well, this is a letter sent of the forensic team Tom Grange who signed the letter, and it relates to a loss of an artifact. If you can just go quickly through the letter and see what it is about, and I will tell you that in September 2001 the OTP investigators checked 25 artifacts located in Zeleni Jadar 6 and took them for comparison with the samples or, rather, took them to the warehouse in Kravica in order to establish whether they can be related to the Kravica warehouse. And it says here that artifact ZJ06/120A had a piece of -- was piece of concrete, and after checking it was established that it did not match any -- anything that was possible to be found in the area, around the warehouse, but after that a storm took place and this artifact had gone missing and cannot be located again. So my question for you is, did you ever hear about this from the OTP? Did any of your colleagues or your predecessors hear about the loss of an artifact discovered in Zeleni Jadar 6 and which was compared with the samples from the Kravica warehouse, and it was -- it turned out that no match could be made, and that subsequently this artifact was misplaced? Have you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I hear of this story from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The fact that a piece of concrete with colour white existed in Zeleni Jadar and that no match could be found in Kravica --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- means that it could be related to other locations? And, of course, had this artifact been preserved, we could have conducted additional investigation in order to find whether there are any other locations where bodies from Zeleni Jadar had been buried.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just correct the transcript. This was definitely my last question, but in transcript on page 29, line 6, it says [In English] The locations from where bodies from -- [Interpretation] Let me just repeat: Some other locations from which the bodies buried in Zeleni Jadar could have originated. And after this, I would like to say that I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Janc, did you wish to comment any further on Mr. Lazarevic's question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to add that, yes, that's the case, most probably, as explained, and we established here that in Glogova there were also bodies from the other locations than Kravica, so meaning around -- from Bratunac and the places we have been discussing here, so that's the case. That can be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good day. My name is Natacha Fauveau-Ivanovic, and I represent my client, and I have a few questions concerning Potocari. This is the grave which was found in a field in Potocari which you have noted in annex A of the report, and for the minute this is a document P4490, page 34 in English, and 51, B/C/S. Can we agree that the six persons -- well, if you find -- if you look on hard copy, page 29 of the annex, annex A. Do you agree that the six persons whose remains were found in that grave had been accurately identified?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like now to show you Evidence P514, page 8. P4514. Page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to ask that this page not be broadcast since it contains names. I need the person listed under 6. It's a little bit lower down on the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that the person listed at point 6 is one of the persons whose remains were found in the Potocari grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document is a document that was supplied to the Office of the Prosecutor by ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the top of the document for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This document was provided to the OTP by the BiH authorities by the Tuzla Prosecutor's Office, I guess, or Tuzla cantonal court, so and this document was provided to them by the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, thank you for this added detail. Can we go back now to number 6. Well, you see the manuscript mentioned, the handwritten mentioned next to number 6, which is circled.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this mention means, which in B/C/S means "no"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it possible, therefore, that this mention could mean that this identification is not confirmed or not confirmed with certainty?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about it what does it mean because it's -- no, I don't know the answer for this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it a fact that you have no knowledge about the cause of death of persons found in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did receive autopsies reports where I think there were no cause of death listed on these reports, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to confirm what you've just said, can we show the witness document P3488. Sorry, 3485. My mistake. That will be page 1 in English, 12 in B/C/S. And I would like you to avoid broadcasting this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, this is a report you are talking about, in fact, and we can indeed say that cause of death is not ascertained; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is as I call them autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And one doesn't know, either, when the person was killed; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can't say from these documents anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau [Microphone not activated] ... Did you say they were killed?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When these persons met their death. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And can we agree to say that we don't know the location where these persons died either?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you a document P3159A. This is also a document which should not be broadcast publicly. Can we go to page 188.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the second part of the document you saw earlier. I assume that you also saw this part of the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And is it correct that the list which follows on succeeding pages -- subsequent pages, rather, contains the names of persons who were identified but were not to be found in the list of persons disappeared or killed after the Srebrenica events of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the case. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to go to the next page, and could we go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a short time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, yes. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm what I just said, we have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc. I really am not going to be very long with you, and I'd like, really, to take you back to Ljubljana and call upon your expertise as a Slovenian police officer that you were telling us about the other day in terms of crowd assessment.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You intrigued me and caused me to embark upon a little research. If the average man sits cross-legged on the floor, he occupies about a square metre of floor space, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And, in fact, and we know this from -- if we imagine an assembly of school children standing up, a human being doesn't occupy much less floor space if he stands up because the width of the body is determined by the shoulders. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So if we have an area of about 10 metres by 10 metres, and people are seated in there wall to wall, you would expect to fit in there about 100 people.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, one of the things that hasn't changed very much between 1995 and today is the size and capacity of buses used for public transport. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the sort of buses with which you would have been familiar with the former Yugoslavia in 1995, much as they would today, have a passenger capacity of about 50 people.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'd agree that if you put on a bus a driver and some guards to keep people apart in the aisles, you are not going to be able to exceed that capacity by very much, are you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them can now sustain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But not very many.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you have 50 seats or thereabouts, and then you can fit -- I don't know how many people, but you can fit a quite amount of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. But if you wanted to move 5.000 people, you'd need something like 100 buses, wouldn't you, if you were going to do it in one convoy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably you calculated this number, yes. That's then the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if you only had 50 buses, in one convoy you would probably only move 2 to 2 and a half thousand, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Have you been to the detention sites in the Zvornik area? That's Orahovac, Petkovci, Rocevic, Pilica, and the Pilica Dom.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have visited most of them -- or all of them but Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask you, then, to look at a selection of plans, and it's 7D929, and we'll go from the back forward. So we'll start at the last page, which is page 6 in the B/C/S and page 7 in the English. I better inquire, do you read Cyrillic, or would you prefer to look at the English, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not that good in Cyrillic. I would rather in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Me neither. Thank you. Well, we'll go forwards, then. If we start with page 1. Do you recognise this as being a floor plan of the ground floor of the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you've been there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do the measurements on that plan setting out the size of the ten rooms on the ground floor approximately accord with your recollection of that building?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were those -- were the plans of that building ever obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor, or was that building ever measured by that office?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of this particular building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But anyway, we can see that there are ten rooms on the ground floor according to the plan with a square metreage of 491.58. And that would be about right, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Janc, you remember how at the Petkovci school you go up the stairs, and the classrooms are all on the front of the building. Does that accord with your recollection of that building on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the nine rooms there, albeit it some of them small cupboards and things, have a total square metreage of 362 and a little bit. Would that about right, the area of the first floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's go to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the one place you haven't been to. This is Rocevic. Have you seen photographs of it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know where that school is and how it looks like from outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you would agree, would you, that the -- what we in English would call the gym or the sports hall is about 12 metres by 23.75 metres as is set out there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that that added together to a little storeroom on the side gives that building an area of 310 metres and a little bit.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go to page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this is the Pilica Dom or Pilica Cultural Centre. You've been there, have you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'll confirm that it's a room that really is in two parts, a flat area and then a stage.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that would appear to you to be correctly measured there, including the stage area at about 223 square metres.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We'll go on to page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've been to Grbavci or Orahovac, the school there, have you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you've seen the, as I say again in English, what we'd call the gym or the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And not dissimilar to the other gym we were looking at, together with a little storeroom on the side, that has an area of 308 metres odd. That would be about right from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And last but not least, page 6 in the B/C/S, page 7 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This really was the purpose of my first question about people sitting cross-legged on the floor. This is the Pilica school. I can't remember; did you say whether you had been there or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He said he hadn't been to Rocevic only, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. That's really helpful. I'd forgot that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the smallest of the areas, about 180 square metres. Do you recall that being a smaller place than the others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I hope you'll take my summary of this. We've looked at 26 separate rooms there with a total area of 1.875 square metres. By all means, you know, I'll run back through them, but I've added them up. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you also accept that if there were only something like 50 buses available and they only made one journey and prisoners were housed in these detention sites we've looked at, it's unlikely that much more than 2.000 people were moved from Bratunac to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I can provide you with the number. I can agree that it's only 2.000 of them, 50 buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Soljan, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I think about 15 minutes. That should be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit 4531 on e-court, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Mr. President. Before my colleague begins her re-examination, I've been reading the last answer from the witness to my colleague's, Mr. Haynes, cross-examination, and I'm not sure I understand the answer as it stands. Does he agree with the proposition that no more than 2.000 were taken to there, or is he saying the opposite? I think he does agree that no more than 2.000, but I'd like that to be clear on the record, Mr. President, before my colleague begins her re-exam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. I think that is a very good point to make, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Janc, do you still have the transcript in front of you, page 39?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have. I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You've heard Mr. Bourgon. What is your comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My comment is opposite as it says, as it is written here, so that I cannot agree, because basic calculation if there is 50 buses and then 50 people on each bus, then it's I think 2.500 at least, so but as I explained in one bus there can be fitted more than only 50 people. I think it's 50 seats on each bus, but you can fit more in one bus, so I don't agree with this figure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the capacity of the rooms of the schools?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be a little bit more difficult question for me. I'm not able to assess how many people can fit in each of these facilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed, Ms. Soljan. Probably you didn't hear me because you are not wearing the headphone. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Your Honour. I was just waiting for the photo to appear. Page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, this is a depiction of a square metre and three people sitting cross-legged in that amount of space. Does this image fit with your understanding of the events or the situation of the victims in Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you believe it isn't a leading question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I don't believe that it's a leading question. I'm simply asking him whether he think that this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just ask him for his comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you comment on this picture knowing that it represents 1 square metre?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it from here, it is -- yeah. I believe that it is 1 square metre, and, yeah, that's how I understand the situation was on the ground at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In other words, that it is possible for up to three people to fit in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's -- again, I mean, this is what the kind of question you shouldn't put. You are giving the -- let's move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, have you been to Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Have you ever been --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to object at this point. This has nothing to do with the cross-examination that I have in relation to Kravica warehouse about number of people that were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not yours, but maybe it's a follow-up to what Mr. Haynes, the line of questions that Mr. Haynes -- let's proceed. Yes, go ahead, if you could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Anyway, in such a situation maybe my colleague could ask general questions, not particularly related to Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Can you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was there several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And are you aware of any other members of the investigation team having been at the Kravica warehouse as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of many of my colleagues have been there already.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Tomasz Blaszczyk was at that Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite sure he was there several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that he has measured the Kravica warehouse and has drawn up a sketch of those dimensions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, that he measured it, but he was not the only one who measured the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, this exhibit is not in e-court, so I would ask that it be placed on ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And again -- I would also like to state again that this is beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you know the particular rule that does not necessarily limit, and jurisprudence. I mean, it's within our discretion. And you weren't the only one who cross-examined this witness. Yes, let's have it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, but I cannot see any indication that this these three gentleman sit inside 1 square metre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's a visual perception that we can all make. Okay? I mean, one could also not sit in that particular position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but again, it's a question for us to look at the picture and draw our own conclusions, and you can do the same. No further comments on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What I can say is there are additional photos within that exhibit where we can also show it from a slightly different perspective if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's your problem or your decisions. We are not going to ask for any further photos unless you feel the need to provide us with more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go back to Exhibit 4931 for a moment, please. 4531, I apologise. The previous page, page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you comment on what you see in this photo, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two men sitting inside that square, which it seems to be 1 square metre, so two men sitting in ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to Exhibit 4529, which is on ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell by looking at this document what this document is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the declaration of my colleague Tomasz Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at paragraph 3, can you please read it out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On March 30, 2007, I visited the Kravica warehouse and measured the inside and outside of the warehouse sections which were accessible to me. I made a rough sketch at the time with my measurements in metres."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And the next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On May 4, 2009, I made a sketch for court purposes based on my measurements and sketch from March 30, 2007."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to object to this line of questioning. Is Mr. Blaszczyk testifying through this witness? If they want information through a witness, Mr. Blaszczyk, he should be here to talk about this, but not this witness to enter the information of the testimony of another investigator. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And one more issue, maybe, that I would also like to raise. Here we can see that it was prepared on May 4, 2009, which means yesterday, and my learned colleague couldn't have known what topic would Mr. Haynes raise in his cross-examination, so it was prepared in advance without me raising any issue regarding the measurements and number of people that can fit in some space.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the issue has arisen, so let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In addition, I can respond to the fact that the very issue of how many people were inside the Kravica warehouse and how many people then may have ended up from Kravica warehouse in any of the Glogova or other secondary graves was raised by the Borovcanin Defence, with all due respect, for hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would really like to make a very clear distinction. Not at any moment did I ask any question about how many people were actually at Kravica warehouse. We were discussing the issue of grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but as I said, you are not the only one who cross-examined the witness. So what we have now is a re-examination by the Prosecution presumably addressing points raised by any one of you, any one of the Defence teams that cross-examined, and Mr. Haynes did ask a specific question, how many people can fit in 1 square metre, or how much space does one person occupy within 1 square metre. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't want to cause trouble, but can we just have some providence for the photographs. Were they likewise taken yesterday, and if so, can we see the people in them?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Excuse me? What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Providence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yeah, who took the photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who took these photos, when and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- when and where, and who were the people in them?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Average-size men are the people who are inside it, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think I can test that, but just tell us when it was taken and by whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: It was taken -- it was indeed taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we please have him address the Court instead of being rude to my young colleague. I hate to stand up like this, but this has got to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Manners haven't been lacking in this courtroom, so let's not make a mountain out of a molehill or raise a storm in a tea-cup. Let's proceed. These are ultimately matters that we will use our own discretion. I mean, I look at these two guys. One has got his knees more or less together, the other one his legs wide open, and they are sitting next to one another. They could have an arm around the other guy's shoulder. I mean, there are many things, factors that one can take into consideration. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we go to the next page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
