utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us what this exhibit depicts or what this picture depicts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the measurement of Kravica warehouse, inside of it, what was written by Tomasz Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can you please read out for the Court what the amount of square metres in the room on the right side in the direction of Konjevic Polje is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Section 1, I can see it's 280.13 square metres. Then below that, you have another number, 262.5 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And on the left side in the room in the direction of Bratunac, can you tell us -- can you read out for the Court how many square metres that room contains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 327 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And does this roughly correspond to the dimensions that you have seen in the course of visiting the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be -- I did not measure it, but it could correspond, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment, Ms. Soljan. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The witness has just confirmed that he did not make these measurements, that these measurements simply could correspond it to what he saw. And, Mr. President, I would like you to rule, please, on my earlier objection that this witness is testifying on the basis of information obtained by another investigator, and we feel that this is inappropriate. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, do you wish to comment --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Mr. Bourgon? Do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Simply to say that hearsay evidence is admissible in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not hearsay evidence. Anyway, let me consult with my colleagues because I think it's an issue that can easily be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, as I anticipated, consultations with my colleagues confirmed what I thought in the first place, that this is nothing out of the ordinary or unusual. We've been doing this all the time. Reference has been made, for example, to the cadastre by one of the Defence teams to measurements, other measurements of other places by another Defence team, and at the end of the day it's a question of how much weight we are going to give to the statements of the witness based, insofar as they are based on conclusions drawn or measurements drawn or facts stated by others. So let's proceed. There's nothing unusual in the way we are proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we please go to Exhibit 4491, page 251, not to be broadcast, please. This would be page R0657797, pages 251, please, in e-court. And could we please close it in some more so we see the centre of the page with the case ID KA01-110BP, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, as you recall, we were discussing in the last few days -- you were testifying in the last few days about a tooth found at the Kravica warehouse and re-associations in the Zeleni Jadar 2 secondary mass grave. If you look at the case ID connected to the KA01-110BP case ID, the tooth found at the Kravica warehouse. The case ID immediately below it states ZJA04 SRE002, gen bon (LF2). Mr. Janc, did you know that LF means left femur?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that, but I was assuming that that's the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go one line down or one row down to ZJA -- case ID ZJA04 SRE002 D-LH 4. Do you know, Mr. Janc, that LH means left humerus?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Janc, in the last few days, there's also been talk about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One second, please. Those two questions, I've let them do it, but those were two leading questions were not appropriate at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But I would just like to tell my colleague that I will object very next time when she puts these kind of questions to Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, but you appreciate we didn't hear any objection at the time. So let's proceed. But you are forewarned now. I mean, you've given advance notice of new objections. So you need to formulate your question somewhat differently now if you are proceeding along the same line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, in the last few days, Mr. Janc, you have looked at exhibits 1D1362, 1D1363, 1D1364, and these were certificates that had been sent to the OTP by the BiH Ministry of Defence correcting the dates initially appearing in the Bosnian list of missing or dead. Let's briefly take a look at an additional related certificate, and that's Exhibit 1D1365, please. I don't believe this is the correct document. Could we try again. 1D1365. It should be ERN 0360-4920. 4921, I apologise. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No broadcast, I assume?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janc, I'd just like you to note the name of the individual for yourself, and can you tell out loud for the record what date he is said to have disappeared?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Disappeared on 11 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have Exhibit 4528, and it should not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, this is a table that includes the names of those four individuals which we've just listed in the above 1D exhibits, and it summarises the most recent ICRC and ICMP data. Can you tell us looking at the date of disappearance, according to the ICRC list, when are these individuals reported as missing by the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First one is 13th of July; the third one is 11th of July; the fourth one is 13th of July; and the last one is 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And according to the ICMP data available on this spreadsheet, can you tell us what graves these individuals are found in?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the first one, I can say this one is coming out from other section, so I did not find out where this particular individual was found, so it is within other section in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we don't have the exact place of the grave-site. So the second and the third ones, they were found in Bljeceva secondary grave number 2. The fourth one was found in Kamenica 10; that means Cancari number 10, Cancari Road number 10, secondary mass grave. And the last one, that one was found in Cancari Road number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you recall for us, individuals coming out of graves such as Cancari 10 and Cancari 3, what execution site or primary grave are these individuals coming from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Cancari 10, the execution site would be Branjevo or Pilica. Then for Cancari number 3, this one is related to Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janc, for your analysis, for purposes of your report, what is more reliable, an ABiH list of dates of disappearance or even ICRC list or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I object to this question. It is fact witness, and he is not authorised to give his assessment of reliability of any evidence here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm asking him specifically for the purposes of the analysis that was done for his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. But restrict your question to that and your answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that it was included in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. He will tell us. He is best place to answer the question, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I actually have not finished my question, Your Honours, so if I could just finish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay. Then finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So I will just reread what I said and then continue. For purposes of your report, Mr. Janc, which is more reliable, an ABiH list of dates of disappearance or even ICRC dates of disappearance or the graves out of which a person is coming?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say the ICRC list is the most reliable for the purposes of my report, then also the list of ICMP, and also the graves. These are three sources most reliable, but I would like to say that ICRC list was made up in 1995, so where -- when the evidence were fresh, but the list from the ABiH, as we can see from these certificates, they were made up in 2004, so it is -- which is ten years later, so that's why I say that this data, this ICRC data are more reliable for my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And a final question, Mr. Janc. As a final matter, I'd like to clarify your testimony from yesterday with respect to one particular question. You were asked at transcript 33636, line 17 to 22: "It's without a doubt, isn't it, that the path report does not exclude or rule out any of the possibilities that I'm suggesting that the numbers that you are giving us are indeed inflated and include individuals who died as a result of sustaining injuries from land-mines, self-inflicted wounds, and/or injuries from legitimate combat engagements." And your answer was at line 23: "Yes, you are right." Now, Mr. Janc, I'd just like to clarify for the record what your answer entailed because it's answering to a compound question, so I'll just break it out into two. Isn't it without a doubt that the report does not exclude or rule out any of the possibilities that I'm suggesting that the numbers that you've given us are indeed inflated? In other words, does your report contain inflated numbers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And the second question, the report does not exclude or rule out any of the possibilities that I'm suggesting, that the numbers you've given us include individuals who died as a result of sustaining injuries from land-mines, self-inflicted wounds, and/or injuries from legitimate combat engagements. What is your answer to that, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that can be the case also, yes, that the report includes those cases, yes, also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no more questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one question, simple question. Mr. Janc, your report is the first one that the analysis of DNA connection; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I'm wondering whether you can off the top of your head give me the number of the individuals that were found in the graves that have a DNA connection in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can. The total number of those individuals is 472 or -- around 470 individuals have different connections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That number is referred to the individual that have the -- whose DNA connection have been found, but I'm referring to the graves, so if you have at least found a connection that two graves can be said to have some DNA connections. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So if you add the numbers of individuals that were found in those graves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I don't understand, Your Honour, what -- if you can give me example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of his report, maybe chart. That's P4490. Yes. Let's see the first left, lower, in the bottom, Cancari road and mass graves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For example, Cancari Road 1, Cancari Road 4, Cancari Road 8 does not have any connection with any other grave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So my question was whether you can give the number off the top of your head if we exclude all those graves which that do not have any connection with another grave? We can do the mathematics ourselves, can we?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can, Your Honour. But I can give you the exact number from the top of my head now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Stole? Mr. Janc, that brings us to the end of your testimony. I thank you very much for having given us your testimony and your time. I hope we won't need you any further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Documents? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are submitting the documents that have been circulated to you, including these last four documents that I tendered in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. I was going to ask you that. Any objections? Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your indulgence, I'll be articulating our objection to P4529.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P -- one moment because I was looking at the wrong one. We don't have the Prosecution list. What you gave us is the Defence list. Did you hear me? I don't have the Prosecution list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: We have circulated it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I will try to find it amongst -- yes, okay. We may have received one earlier from our staff, obviously, but I don't see it either. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we have -- sorry for the confusion. We have five pages, and you are making submissions, Mr. Gosnell, relation to which one, which document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me follow from the transcript. P4529. Yes. Okay. It's the second of the four documents used in redirect. Sketch with measurements of Kravica warehouse is what you are referring to. Yes, let's hear the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There are several grounds of objection. The first ground and one of the main reasons why I'm standing to address you instead of my colleague relates to the scope of the re-opening that you granted. Paragraph 49 of the Prosecution motion concerning Investigator Janc's testimony stated as follows: "The Prosecution seeks to call OTP Investigator Dusan Janc to introduce updated information relating to Dean Manning's November 2007 report. The proposed evidence comprises a report prepared by Janc, the documents, reports and data upon which it is based, and his viva voce testimony." That was the scope of the re-opening that you granted, and my colleague Mr. Lazarevic did not in any way go beyond the four corners of what you had granted re-opening for. So we would suggest to you, Mr. President, that we do not object to the photo, P4531, because as you rightly pointed out, that may have been raised or put in issue by one of the other Defence teams, and nor would we object if the Prosecution had sought to contest some of the sketches used by my colleague. But what we have here is something very different. The Prosecution is trying to get a sketch in about a site that was not mentioned by any of the other Defence teams and that directly concerns my client and that was not raised by our Defence team on cross-examination. Indeed, it was not raised by any Defence team on cross-examination. So what we have, I would suggest to you, Mr. President, is the Prosecution going far beyond the scope of cross when you really look at what was being contested in cross-examination in conjunction with what was granted on re-opening. And the second point that I would just beg your indulgence to make before you, Mr. President, is that although it's true that hearsay is not inherently inadmissible, I believe that there is case law on precisely this type of document being brought into evidence. I don't have that case law with me, but I believe that this type of hearsay is -- has been ruled inadmissible by other Trial Chambers, and I can't tell you right now whether that's true, but I believe it to be the case. And I would suggest to you, Mr. President, that this is just a question of simple fairness. What we have is a document being put in that describes the dimensions of the Kravica warehouse during re-examination of a witness who was supposed to be testifying about forensic evidence when that issue was not raised by our Defence team. Very simply, Mr. President, we have no opportunity to challenge this evidence, to show that it might be incorrect, or even for that matter to ask questions to the witness. So on those grounds, Mr. President, we strongly object to this document coming into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Shortly, briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Very briefly. This is redirect, and not just one but multiple teams have brought up the issue of numbers. Mr. Haynes brought specifically the issue of square metreage inside a building, but the Borovcanin team I find is very incorrect in saying that they did not raise the issue of numbers. In fact, the entire cross-examination of Mr. Janc consisted of calculating out numbers in the Glogova grave and any of the graves that are said to be related to Kravica and thereby related directly to how many people were in the Kravica warehouse. So that is my argument. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me see if I need to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, as I anticipated, I barely needed to consult my colleagues on this. You seem to have forgotten completely, at the end of the day, because the bottom line is we went there. We went on site, and we had the area measured. So at the end of the day, you have nothing new here. So as I said earlier on, it's still a storm in a tea cup. With regard to your other point raised, it's faulty reasoning, it's bad reasoning to refer to the limited scope for which we admitted the production of this witness when in actual fact in the course of the testimony, particularly during some of the cross-examinations, the window was -- or the door was widened and the range extended to include other matters that were not originally within the limited scope of the purpose for which we admitted this witness. But I'm not blaming you, but I think each one should consider whether it's a case of self-inflicted. So objection is overruled. The document is -- unless we hear further objections to the admission of the lists, Prosecution list of documents? We hear none. So those are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry. I object to 4531, the photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. On what ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, they are described in the list that's just been circulated as four photos showing numbers of average-sized people fitting inside the space of 1 square metre. Firstly, only two were used in evidence; secondly, the commentary in the description is completely unproven. There's no evidence that they are average sized or, indeed, that they were sitting within a metre, and we invited providence to be shown during the course of the testimony, and although Mr. McCloskey got upset with me, they never did. So therefore, the objection is that they are unproven. There is no evidence as to the facts asserted in the description. They are of minimal probative value in any event because you will recall the evidence of how people said they were seated in various detention sites, and you'll recall the evidence of Mr. Janc himself that the average man takes up 1 square metre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and I could also add that there is no evidence that what is alleged to be 1 square metre is indeed 1 square metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I did say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. We don't need any comments on this. At the end of the day, we will use our judgement. I mean, we may or may not need photos, but at the end of the day it's not the photo which is going to the determine the amount of persons that can fit in a particular gym or room or garage or store or classroom. So your objection is of insignificant value or merit, has insignificant merit in our opinion, Mr. Haynes, and the photographs will remain there, and we will use our own discretion at the end of the day. Yes. Popovic list of documents has been circulated. We have 5, 10, 15, I think. Any objections? Some of them will remain under seal, Mr. Registrar, please, almost all of them, actually. Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: We have no objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No objections from the other Defence teams. They are admitted. Beara list, four documents. Any objections from the Prosecution? My only question to you, Mr. Ostojic, is that in the first three of these four documents it just says statement of, statement of, statement of, and you mention three individuals. Are you proposing to admit the entire statement for evidence of its content or not? Because at the end of the day, you read out from these statements to the witness. What you read out is in the transcript, and to be honest with you, I have a question as to whether we need to have them in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'd like them into evidence, Your Honour. That's why we put them on the exhibit list, and given the Court's ruling on the Prosecution's evidence or documents, we believe that the same rules should apply and those documents should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but the understanding is that they are not being tendered for proof of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I think in conjunction with the witness's testimony, they actually are, but we can look at that and evaluate that at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'll give you the floor shortly, Ms. Soljan. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just for the Court's information, 2D667 apparently has already been admitted as a 92 bis statement, P2203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you for that. It seems to be the case. Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: That is indeed the case, but we nevertheless object to the other two statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On which ground?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- because they have already been read into the record, and there is -- it has been practice so far not to admit such statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further comments from the other Defence teams? None. I need to consult with my colleagues here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our decision is to admit these other two documents, 669, 702, but along the lines of our previous decisions, in other words, don't expect us to allow in a procedure by which unsworn testimony is admitted in this -- of third parties is admitted in this way. So we know exactly for which purpose they are being admitted. Next, the Borovcanin Defence -- Nikolic had no documents. Borovcanin Defence team, there are four documents that I have in front of me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. These are the four documents that we would like to offer to be tendered into evidence, with one remark: 4D754 should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, and there was one which was not translated at yet, no, or is it not here? It isn't here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not here. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No objections from the other Defence teams? None. They are so admitted. Last list I have is from Ms. -- you had no -- okay, Ms. Fauveau had no documents to tender, and the Pandurevic team has only got one document which they wish to tender, which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's the plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, 7929. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes -- one moment. I need to consult on something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the time being, we do not have anything on the basis of which we can plan our scheduling ahead as far as testimony is concerned. There are two things pending in the pipeline. One depends on Mr. Zivanovic giving -- updating information on the evidence the Popovic Defence team plans details thereof so that we'll know whether we need any sittings for that. And the other will depend on a decision which we are in the process of finalising and which will be communicated to you shortly. But let's start with Mr. Zivanovic. We are talking of the Bisina and evidence you would like to bring forward, and Dusan -- what was it, Dunjac --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dusan -- yeah. Your Honour, so we submitted three Rule 92 bis witness statements, and the Prosecution agreed not to call these witnesses for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which ones? Bisina?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Bisina witnesses. Our motion to call Mr. Kosoric and our expert Ms. Evuga [phoen] is pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that is another one pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Our deadline to submit our Rule 92 bis witness statements for Professor Dunjic and Professor Stojkovic expires I believe next week, next week, on this day next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the preparation of expert report for Mr. Rodic is underway. I believe that it will be done next week as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course we haven't handed down the decision as yet, but in -- as regards bringing back Mr. Kosoric here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We sought to bring him here to refute the testimony of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are fully aware of why you would like Mr. Kosoric back here. We are just sort of giving you an advance, some kind of formal advance notice by suggesting that you inquire about his availability so that we will have an indication as to when to hear his evidence. But the decision will be forthcoming shortly. It will be officialised or formalised in a proper decision, but you are being given advance notice to expect a positive outcome as far as that witness is concerned. We need to know when he is available because we also need to plan the sittings, and as you know, we have to plan sittings with other Trial Chambers, and there are logistic problems that have to be addressed. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do it very soon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Actually when I say recalled, it's the wrong description of the facts, but we will be calling him. Anything else before we rise? Well, expect a few decisions shortly. There are several small matters pending in addition to the major ones, and we will dispose of them in the course of the week. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.25 p.m.
